 Payton Pritchard (eye) is questionable to play against the Hornets on Friday.
 Pritchard has an eye abrasion that could prevent him from suiting up against Charlotte. Mike Conley would likely operate as the Celtics’ backup point guard if Pritchard isn’t available, though that will likely only be in a limited capacity.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Payton Pritchard (shoulder) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Pritchard was listed as questionable with a shoulder injury, but has since been ruled in for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. He’s coming off a rough game where he was 0-of-7 from the field with four points in 30 minutes against the Rockets Monday. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard (shoulder) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Pritchard most recently played 30 minutes off the bench in Monday’s loss to the Rockets. If he can’t play Wednesday, Mike Conley could slide into the back end of the Celtics’ rotation, but that isn’t guaranteed. Conley should not be rostered in redraft leagues. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard accumulated 30 points (9-of-17 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Given his performance in Boston’s two comfortable wins over the Bulls this week, Pritchard clearly enjoys playing against them. After putting up 28 points on Monday, the Celtics guard came off the bench to record his first 30-point game of the season. Over five games, Pritchard has been inconsistent scoring-wise, alternating between double- and single-digit outputs. He’ll look to buck that trend when the Celtics face the Magic on Sunday. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard led the Celtics with 28 points (10-of-16 FGs), one rebound, four assists, two steals and seven three-pointers in a 134-99 win over the Bulls on Monday. 
 Pritchard had a rough performance on Friday, where he was held to just four points on 1-of-5 FGs. He surpassed his total for points and three-pointers through their first two games in this game alone. Pritchard is more than capable of producing to this level, though it won’t come consistently. However, he’ll continue to play a significant role off the bench and see plenty of usage. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard tallied seven points (3-of-11 FGs), three rebounds, 11 assists and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Hornets. 
 Pritchard, who signed a two-year, $44.2 million extension on Tuesday, racked up a game-high 11 assists on Wednesday. He’s coming off his most productive season to date, posting career-best averages in points, rebounds, and assists. Pritchard finished last season as a top-100 player in 12-team formats, and fantasy managers can reasonably expect similar production in 2026-27. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with the Celtics that includes a mutual option in 2029-30. 
 The six-year vet has seen his role blossom from rotational microwave-scorer in Year 1 to key piece of Boston’s 2023-24 title run and 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year. Pritchard enjoyed the most productive season of his career in 2025-26, posting career-highs with 17 points, 3.9 rebounds and 5.2 assists across 32.6 minutes. Jayson Tatum is back in the mix to open the season, but Pritchard should remain a key scorer and playmaker, and the extension he signed is a reflection of the team’s confidence in him as a foundational franchise player. 
 Payton Pritchard 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Payton Pritchard poured in a game-high 25 points (7-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds and seven assists over 24 minutes in Saturday’s lopsided preseason win over the 76ers. 
 Boston’s bench looked to be in midseason form with Pritchard carrying the bulk of the scoring workload for the non-Tatum unit as he finished the opening half with a team-high 15 points. He drained 5-of-8 attempts from three-point range and finished second on the Celtics behind Jayson Tatum with 12 shot attempts. Pritchard remains a streaky shooter capable of putting up huge scoring numbers when he’s in a groove. He’ll be a top-100 range selection in fantasy drafts this fall. 
 Mike Conley 
 BOS 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Mike Conley has agreed to a one-year deal with the Celtics, reports ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 Conley’s contract will pay him the veteran minimum. His arrival in Boston puts an end to a four-year tenure in Minnesota during which he averaged 9.0 points, 4.6 assists and shot 41 percent from behind the three-point line. Conley will serve as guard depth with the Celtics behind Derrick White and Payton Pritchard. 
 Ayo Dosunmu 
 MIN 
 Guard 
 #13 
 Ayo Dosunmu, Anthony Edwards, Jaden McDaniels, Julius Randle and Rudy Gobert will start Sunday’s Game 4 against the Spurs. 
 After coming off the bench in his return to action on Friday, Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup for Sunday night. As a result, Mike Conley will head to the bench and could fall out of the rotation entirely. With Dosunmu available, Conley played four minutes in Friday’s Game 3 defeat despite remaining in the starting lineup. 
 Mike Conley 
 MIN 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Mike Conley recorded 12 points (4-of-8 FGs), two rebounds, six assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s Game 1 win over the Spurs. 
 Due to injuries, the Timberwolves have relied on Conley far more than anticipated at the start of the postseason. The 38-year-old point guard shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and did not commit a turnover in his 24 minutes. Conley’s playing time should remain in the 24-26 minute range moving forward, especially with Anthony Edwards (knee) back in action.

 Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.
 Booker has had a few rough performances early on this season, but this has been an excellent two-game stretch for him. He has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games, and he set a new season high for assists, steals and three-pointers in this one. Outside of a dud game against the Thunder, Booker has been excellent this season. He’ll continue to have the ball in his hands, and if he’s shooting the ball this well, the results will continue to be great for fantasy managers.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Miles Bridges stuffed the stat sheet on Thursday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), 13 rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Magic.
 With both Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach in foul trouble, Bridges was able to step up on the glass. He ended up setting a new season high for rebounds in what has been an excellent start to the year for him, especially as of late. Over his last four games, Bridges has averaged 20.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.3 steals, 1.0 block and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 51.8 percent from the free throw line. He has been fantastic in fantasy basketball and will look to stay hot against the Rockets on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dillon Brooks posted a full line on Thursday with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs), one rebound, one assist, two steals, one block and four three-pointers against the Magic.
 Brooks’ scoring has dropped off this season, but he has made up for it with improved efficiency. However, he was able to do both in this game, which led to his best scoring performance of the season. Brooks has shot at least 55 percent from the floor in three of his last four games, which has helped his value in nine-category leagues. He likely won’t continue to shoot this well, but he certainly has the hot hand right now.

 Oso Ighodaro started on Thursday and finished with two points (1-of-2 FGs), five rebounds, one assist and one block against the Magic.
 Head coach Jordan Ott made the call to replace Khaman Maluach with Ighodaro in the starting unit. Unfortunately, Ighodaro found himself in foul trouble throughout the game, which prevented him from providing much value. Ighodaro is worth considering as a waiver wire pickup, even if this first game as a starter was rough. He won’t do much scoring, but he’s a strong passer for a big man and has five blocks over his last three games.

 Tristan da Silva provided a boost off the bench with 18 points (6-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
 All season long, da Silva has been a solid source of offense off the bench for Orlando, and he was able to provide that once again in this game. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been able to provide much outside of points and three-pointers, outside of a singular double-digit rebounding game last week. Aside from that night, da Silva hasn’t had more than four rebounds in a game. He’ll continue to score, but noting else will come consistently.

 Wendell Carter Jr. led the Magic with 27 points (10-of-12 FGs), 13 rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
 Carter has had a few 20-point games this season and a few 10-rebound games, but he hadn’t done both at the same time until this game. He also set new season highs for both categories in what ended up being his best performance of the season. WCJ has been excellent to start the year, though he has had a four poor games mixed in.  Franz Wagner recorded a double-double on Thursday with 15 points (7-of-13 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, 15 assists, four steals and six turnovers in a 117-104 loss to the Suns.
 With both Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) out, Wagner has stepped up as the team’s primary playmaker. That has led to some incredible assist numbers this season. He matched his previous career high for dimes last week before setting it last weekend. He set a new career high for assists once again in this game. Wagner has taken on a lot of responsibility on both ends of the floor, but he hasn’t excelled as a scorer. Still, he has been productive in other categories while trying to keep Orlando afloat until they get healthier.
 -  Noah Rubin
